en: A memorial submitted regarding the catalog of Dharma implements and other items requested by the Abbot of Insan-sa,
by the śramaṇa Wonhaeng, who returned from his studies in Tang China: "Wonhaeng, in the year of Gwimoo (598), received this imperial mandate."
Seeking further instruction,
he traveled beyond the Western Sea to inquire after the Way.
In the twelfth month of that year, he arrived at the city of Chang’an.
On the thirteenth day of the first month of the year Jiwu (1079),
by imperial decree following a memorial, I resided at Qinglong Temple.
It was my good fortune to encounter the Abbot of that temple, the Dharma Master named Yijin, who served as my preceptor for the consecration.
As for Da Weide, he was a disciple of the master Huiguo and a fellow student of Master Yicao, who was a recipient of the Dharma transmission;
he was profoundly learned and well-versed in the Three Teachings.
He was profoundly versed in the five families [of esoteric Buddhism] and served as a pillar of the Dharma;
he was the one upon whom the nation relied. Our complete practice has been made possible by the vast grace of the Holy Court.
The profound compassion of the Master,
which resolves doubts regarding the Great Dharma of the two divisions and awakens one to the secret teachings of the various Honored Ones.
On the second day of the intercalary first month, I received the consecration for the rank of Ācārya.

The Left Street Commissioner of Merit, the Monastic Registrar, the Honored Monk, the Great Virtuous One, and all the disciples of the Vajra Gate gathered at the ritual site together to express their sympathetic joy.
In this Dharma, by contemplating the moon-disc of the mind, one dwells in the stage of an ordinary being while yet possessing the virtues of a Buddha;
by reciting the secret words of the mouth, one bypasses long kalpas and immediately ascends to the rank of Great Enlightenment.
Therefore, Nāgārjuna said:
"If one travels by riding a sheep, it is difficult to reach a distant destination; if one gallops by urging on a horse, one gradually expects to proceed more swiftly."
By mounting the divine vehicle and giving rise to the thought [of awakening], one arrives;
this is the distinction between the Exoteric and the Esoteric.
It is also stated in the Secret Sūtra:
When a son of good family establishes a *bodhimaṇḍa* and practices the recollection of the three mysteries,
within his realm there shall be no calamities of the seven difficulties;
the king and his ministers shall daily increase in merit and longevity.
This is indeed the efficacy of the mantra.
Nevertheless, waves may drench the riverbank,
and wind and rain may drift the ship.
Having crossed that whale-ocean, one returns peacefully to the sacred realm;
this is precisely what can be accomplished through the power of the Sage.
We humbly observe that Your Majesty, the Emperor, surpasses the profound ultimate in merit and excels the primordial chaos in the Way.
He praised Yao’s "Jade Chart" and restored Yu’s great succession;
he felt compassion for the common people and waded through the mud with his feet wet.
Zhongfo entrusted [the task] and passed on the mantle,
so that Your Majesty might cause the Buddha-dharma to flourish;
thus, the śarīra of Maitreya has come from afar, floating upon the waves.
Because Your Majesty has nurtured all within the seas with compassion,
these secret sūtras and dharmas have traveled across the ocean and arrived here from afar.
That these secret teachings have been transmitted is not without reason.
The Tathāgata possesses the power of primordial merit and wisdom;
it is the power of the sustaining grace (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of the intrinsic nature of the *dharmadhātu*.
Thus, Mahāvairocana Tathāgata.
Vajrasattva, the Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna,
and the Bodhisattva Nāgabodhi.
Vajrabodhi Tripiṭaka Master,
Amoghavajra Tripiṭaka Master,
and Preceptor Huiguo.
Master Yicao and Master Yizhen transmitted it to one another in succession.
I have now conferred upon you the complete practice (*pūrṇa-caryā*).
A separate catalog of the sūtras, dharmas, śarīra relics, ritual implements, and other items conferred is provided elsewhere.
I respectfully present these to you; I am deeply apprehensive that my intrusion upon your august presence may cause you offense, and I pray for your forbearance.
Respectfully submitted by the śramaṇa Enkō, with the utmost sincerity and reverence.

On the nineteenth day of the twelfth month of the sixth year of Jōwa, the śramaṇa Enkō, who has returned from his studies in Tang China, presents this memorial in his capacity as the Great Dharma Master Denpō (Dharma-lamp). The Catalogue of Sūtras, Buddha Images, and Ritual Implements Brought Back by the Śramaṇa Enkō from Tang China in the Sixth Year of Jōwa consists of a total of seven items.

The newly requested Mantra scriptures and dharmas comprise twenty-six sections and thirty-three fascicles; additionally, there are three sections and four fascicles of Indic-script texts, including sutras, śāstras, commentaries, and topical expositions of the Exoteric teachings.
The above three categories comprise forty works totaling eighty-eight fascicles.
Altogether, these amount to sixty-nine works totaling one hundred twenty-three fascicles.
Furthermore, there are over three thousand grains of the Buddha’s *śarīra*, along with three types of objects for entrustment: images of the Buddha and diagrams of mandalas.
In total, twelve kinds of ritual implements and sixteen new items have been requested. Regarding the newly requested *Dhāraṇī-sūtra* and *Dharma*:
the *Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the Extraordinary and Most Supreme Golden Wheel Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa*, one fascicle; the *Ritual Manual for the White Parasol Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa*, one fascicle;
the *Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the Ekākṣara-Uṣṇīṣa-Rāja*, one fascicle; and [the manual] based on the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven...
*The Sūtra Spoken at the Assembly of the Heavenly Kings’ Palace*, translated [by Amoghavajra], one fascicle; *The Susiddhi Method*, one part in two fascicles;
*The Sūtra on the Compendium of the True Realm of All Buddhas*, one part in three fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā; *The Ritual Manual of Trailokyavijaya*, one fascicle;
and *The Scripture on the Method for Entering the Maṇḍala and Receiving Empowerment as Taught by the Preceptor Sarvajña to his Vajra Disciple*, one fascicle.
*The Scripture on the Great Accomplishment of the Vajraśrī*, one fascicle; also known as *The Scripture of the Five Eyes*, extracted from *The Scripture of the Vajra Peak*.
*The Ritual for the General Protection of Recitation Across All Sections*, one fascicle.

*The Highest Vehicle Precepts for Receiving the Bodhicitta and the Secret Decisions on the Mind-Ground*, one fascicle. Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha based on the Esoteric Teachings for his disciples.
*Yixing ji zongshi tuoluoni yi zan* (Commentary on the Meaning of Dhāraṇīs by Yixing), one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra by imperial decree.

*Shui zizai jing* (Sūtra of Mastery over Water), one fascicle; also titled *Fo shuo shengzhe manibada tuoluoni pusa tuoluoni jing* (The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Noble Maṇibhadra Bodhisattva Dhāraṇī).
*Kongjie yujia lueshu san-shi qi zun xinyao* (A Brief Exposition of the Essential Heart-Mantras of the Thirty-Seven Deities of the Vajradhātu Yoga), one fascicle; by Amoghavajra.
One fascicle titled *The Three Treasuries’ Exposition of the Garbhadhātu Teachings and the Vajradhātu Vajra Names*, compiled by the Inner Offering Official Yicao;
one work in two fascicles titled *The Sūtra on the Merits of the Parṇaśavarī-Īśvarī Dhāraṇī*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Ratnamegha;
and one fascicle titled *The Praise of the Practices and Vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva*, a bilingual edition in Sanskrit and Chinese with parallel columns for comparison.
*The Sanskrit-Sinitic Text on Merit and the Sequential Order of the Root of All Syllables*, Volume One;
*The Dhāraṇī for the Protection of the Dharma by the Northern King Vaiśravaṇa*, One Scroll;
*The Ritual Manual for the Rules of Maheśvara*, One Scroll, translated separately by the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra; and *Mañjuśrī [Chapter] of the Vajraśekhara Sūtra*.
*The Chapter on the Five-Syllable Heart Dhāraṇī of the Bodhisattva*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Vajrabodhi.
*A Brief Method for the Cultivation and Recitation of the Ārya-mantra of Maitreya Bodhisattva*, one work in two fascicles; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha.
*The Mahāvaipulya Tathāgatagarbha Sūtra*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra. *The Prajñāpāramitā of the Universal Wisdom Treasury Spoken by the Buddha*.
The Heart Sūtra of the Perfection of Wisdom, one fascicle; the Dhāraṇī Sūtra for Deliverance from Suffering and Calamity, one fascicle;
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra; the sixth volume (of) the second part of the Mahāsthāmaprāpta Avalokiteśvara-vikurvaṇa-dhāraṇī-sūtra, two fascicles;
and the Method for Reciting the Eight-Syllable Dhāraṇī of the Great Holy Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci.
*The Sūtra on the Cultivation of Yoga for the Mantra of Uṣṇīṣavijayā*, translated by Śubhakarasiṃha of the Tripiṭaka, two fascicles;
*The Preface to the Mahāvairocana Sūtra*, one fascicle; *Verses on the Five-Syllable Dhāraṇī*, one fascicle;
*The Chapter on the Great Maṇḍala of the Lotus of All Tathāgatas*, one fascicle; and *The Sūtra of Mārīcī*, one fascicle.
*The Sūtra on the Ten Powers Spoken by the Buddha*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on the Wheel of Dedication Spoken by the Buddha*, one fascicle;
*The Sūtra on the Ten Stages Spoken by the Buddha*, nine fascicles; *The Brahma-script Mother of Buddhas Peacock Illustrious Queen Sūtra*, one work in three fascicles;
*A Comparative Glossary of Chinese and Sanskrit Script*, one fascicle. It has taken one or two years to interpret these scripts, making them fit for translation. The above items have newly arrived.

One fascicle of the *Praise of the Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva* (in Sanskrit characters), with Sanskrit and Chinese characters corresponding; one fascicle of the *Siddham* (Sanskrit) script. Although these two works had arrived previously, they were requested to be brought [again] for the purpose of verifying the original texts.
Commentaries and Chapters on the Sūtras and Śāstras of the Exoteric Teachings;
*The Sūtra on the Innate Purity of the Nature of Vajrasamādhi, Neither Destroyed Nor Extinct*, one fascicle (re-imported for the purpose of verifying the original);

*The Sūtra of Adornment for Bodhi*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kumārajīva; the lower fascicle of the *Brahmajāla Sūtra*, calligraphic edition; *The Buddha-Spoken Sūtra on Entering the Realm of the Buddha*.
*Jie jing* (Dhātu-sūtra), one fascicle, two volumes; *Lengqie chao* (Excerpts from the Laṅkāvatāra), one fascicle, five volumes, lacking the first [fascicle];

*Lengqie jing ji yi* (Collected Meanings of the Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra), one fascicle, five volumes; *Lengqie jing da yi zheng cheng chao* (Commentary on the Proof of the Great Meaning of the Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra), one fascicle, two volumes;

*Huayan fajie guan xuanjing* (The Mysterious Mirror of the Huayan Contemplation of the Dharma-realm), one fascicle, composed by Master Chengguan; *Bore xin jing yi* (Meaning of the Heart Sūtra of Prajñā), one fascicle, by Zhikai.
One fascicle of *The Essential Decisions on the Meaning of the Heart Sūtra of Prajñā*, compiled by the Dharma Master;
two fascicles of a commentary on the *Heart Sūtra of Prajñā*; one fascicle of a sub-commentary on the *Commentary on the Heart Sūtra of Prajñā* by Master Jingjue;

one work in two fascicles titled *A Sub-commentary on the Praise and Explanation of the Golden Prajñā Sūtra Based on the Treatise of Bodhisattva Vasubandhu*, compiled by Dharma Master Xiancheng; and [the works of] the śramaṇa of Chongsheng Monastery.
One work in three fascicles: A Commentary on the Mahāyāna Śrī-mahādevī-vajraśekhara-sūtra (Dafoding jing shu) compiled by Lükou; one work in six fascicles:

A Commentary on the Most Victorious Sūtra (Zuisheng jing shu) composed by Master Weiyin; one fascicle: A Commentary on the Amitābha Sūtra (Wéizhèngběn zàiqiúqǐng Āmítuó jīng shu) composed by Master Zhāo; one work:
A Commentary on the Meaning of the *Amitābha Sūtra* According to Circumstances (Āmítuó jīng suíyuán yìcāo) compiled by Master Zhishou. These were collected and presented by [the author].
*Yángjiāxiáng chāo* (Excerpts on Auspiciousness), one fascicle; *Dàoyīn jíjì* (Record of the Collection of Dharma Seals), one fascicle;

*Bǎifǎ míngmén lùn shū* (Commentary on the *Śataśāstra-prakaraṇa*), one fascicle, composed by Dharma Master Zhōng; *Chéng wéishí lùn shū* (Commentary on the *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra*), ten fascicles, composed by Dharma Master Qīngsù;
*Xīnjí bǎifǎ shǒuchāo* (Newly Compiled Hand-Copy of the *Śataśāstra*), six fascicles; *Bǎifǎ lùn yìjù* (Collection of Meanings from the *Śataśāstra*), ten fascicles, composed by Dharma Master Qīngsù.

*Cheng weishi lun shu* (Commentary on the *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra*), ten fascicles, composed by Dharma Master Qing Su. *Fayuan zhulin* (Pearl Forest of the Dharma Garden), one work in ten fascicles, compiled by Dharma Master Dao.
*Bai lun shu* (Commentary on the *Śata-śāstra*), one fascicle, composed by the Śramaṇa Huigao of Mount Emei. *Zhong lun zhigui* (The Essential Meaning of the *Mūlamadhyamaka-kārikā*), one fascicle.
*Bai yu jia tuo* (Hundred Parables in Gāthā Verse), one fascicle, composed by the Inner Palace Attendant, Dharma Master Yilin. *Neiming yi* (Meaning of Inner Science).

*The Mind*, one fascicle; compiled by Dharma Master Daohan, *A Brief Record of the Compendium of Inner Knowledge*, one fascicle; *The Mahāyāna Treatise on Contemplating the Mind*, one fascicle; translated by Dharma Master Xuanzang;
*The Bhikṣu’s Commentary on the Prātimokṣa Sūtra*, one fascicle; composed by the Śramaṇa Daoxuan of Taiyi Mountain;
*A Praise for Rebirth through the Practice of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi Based on the Contemplation Sūtra and Other Texts*, one fascicle; [compiled by] Shan.
*The Praise for the Ritual of Reciting the Sūtras, Practicing the Path, and Vowing to Be Reborn in the Pure Land*, one fascicle in two volumes, composed by Master Daoshi;
*The Minor Śamatha-vipaśyanā*, one volume, composed by Master Shandao;

and *The Dharma Gate of the Merits of the Samādhi of Contemplating the Ocean-like Marks of Amitābha Buddha*, one volume, requested by Yongzhengben and composed by Chan Master Zhiyi of Mount Tiantai—all included.
*Śāśāstra-kārikā-ṭīkā*, one volume in six fascicles, composed by Dharma Master Yuánhuí;

*Kalpa-pariccheda-kārikā*, one volume, composed by Bodhisattva Vasubandhu and translated by Tripiṭaka Master Yìjìng; *Kalpa-pariccheda-kārikā-ṭīkā*, one volume, compiled by Śramaṇa Biànzhì of Fēngshān;
*Nánzōng-dìngshìfēilùn* (Treatise Determining Right and Wrong in the Southern School), one volume, composed by Dúgū Shī of Hénán Fǔ. The above items are hereby manifested.
If there are commentaries on the sutras, śāstras, or treatises that have not yet been transmitted,
or even if they have been transmitted but the text has suffered omissions or errors,
please request that they be brought here.
Buddha relics, more than three thousand grains in total: one hundred grains were entrusted by the Great Virtuous Master and Acharya Yijin of Qinglong Temple;
two hundred and seventy-odd grains were entrusted by the Tripitaka Master Nanda from Central India;
and more than two thousand seven hundred grains were entrusted to the disciple of the Great Virtuous Master Lingxian for transmission and entrustment.
As for the entrusted items: one leaf from a Bodhi tree was placed upon its stem;
the Tripitaka Master Nanda of Central India transmitted a string of agallochum beads to Acharya Yijin;
he [Yijin] transmitted two sets of Sanskrit manuscripts—one set transmitted by the Tripitaka Master Nanda of Central India and one set transmitted by the Venerable Rishi—to the Buddha.

One scroll of a Maṇḍala diagram featuring Buddha images; one scroll of a Garbhadhātu Maṇḍala diagram, inscribed with both Sanskrit and Chinese titles for each honored deity; one scroll of the Maṇḍala of Avalokiteśvara Arulika;
and one statue of Śākyamuni Buddha beneath the Bodhi tree, commissioned by an Indian monk and presented to the Great Tang Emperor for implementation.
One image of the Golden Wheel Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa Cakravartin; one image of the Fire-Head Vajra;
one image of the Vajrakumāra Krodharāja; one image of the Bodhisattva Mahāśrīdevī;
one image of the Bodhisattva Mārīcī; one image of the Mother Hārītī; and one image of the World-Honored One Radiant as Sun and Moon.
One image of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara (Water-Moon) and one image of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra;
these honored images were commissioned as models for the purpose of verifying the original design. I respectfully request them.

Ritual Implements: one single-pronged vajra, one three-pronged vajra, one five-pronged vajra; one three-pronged bell, one five-pronged bell; one wheel; four karma-vajras; four vajra-kīlas; one śataghnī-bell; and one conch shell. The aforementioned items are to be held and offered by the Dharma-transmitting Ācārya as part of the samaya of practice.
Previously, the following items were requested and brought back: various sutras, dharmas, ritual implements, śarīra relics, and commentaries on the exoteric sūtras and śāstras.

Furthermore, although the secret dharma rituals and manuals of the one hundred and twenty-three divisions of the Mantra Vehicle (Shingon) were meticulously examined and verified, they have also been requested and brought back.
The Great Master Kūkai, who first entered Táng China, had already completed his invitation [of these texts] during the Enryaku era;
consequently, they were not included in the catalog.
On the nineteenth day of the twelfth month of the sixth year of Jōwa.

The Record of the Discourse on the Profound Principles of Our Own School between the Japanese National Dharma Master of the Lamp, Great Dharma Master Yuanxing, and the Six Virtuous Monks of the Three Enlightenments, including the Right Street Monk Registrar and Great Virtue in Discourse on the Three Teachings, Dharma Master Tixu.

This was conducted at Qinglong Temple by order of the Imperial Envoy, the General of the Household Qiu, with the six virtuous monks serving as attendants. The names of the participants are listed below.
Within Baoshou Temple, the eminent monk and śramaṇa Changbian was enshrined;
within Zhangjing Temple, the eminent monk and śramaṇa Hongbian of the Chan school was enshrined.
The Great Virtuous Śramaṇa Qi Gao, a lecturer and attendant at Zhaofu Temple;
and the Great Virtuous Śramaṇa Guang Hao, a lecturer and attendant at Xingtang Temple.
Within Yunhwa Temple, the venerable monk Hae-an, a great master of exposition and debate, was enshrined.
Within Cheongnyong Temple, the venerable monk Won-kyeong, a great master of exposition and debate, was enshrined.

The foregoing discourse on the gates of the teachings between the aforementioned Virtuous Ones and the Virtuous Yuanxing, along with the topical outline, has been recorded and submitted for the Imperial perusal.
The fifteenth day of the first month of the fourth year of the Kaicheng era.
